description: Application-layer model under Byzantine sign-flip attack with standard FedAvg and no defence. Demonstrates partial (not catastrophic) degradation — scale=2.0 chosen to avoid NaN overflow at application model's smaller gradient magnitudes.

attack_config.why_scale_2_not_5: Application model has smaller gradient magnitudes than network model due to different class distribution (SQL_injection=1001 samples, much sparser data). Scale=5.0 caused NaN overflow in the application model, breaking the undefended comparison. Scale=2.0 produces measurable degradation without overflow — a more realistic attack scenario.
attack_config.effect_vs_network: Application model does NOT show NaN collapse unlike network model at scale=5.0. The attack causes degradation but the model continues functioning, making this a more nuanced attack demonstration.

defence_config.aggregation: Standard FedAvg — all 10 clients including 2 Byzantine

results.f1_macro_discrepancy_note: 0.471 is the figure quoted in experiment analysis (likely from a mid-run measurement or averaged across later rounds). Round 25 CSV data computes to 0.421. Application model shows high round-to-round variance making any single round less representative than the trend.

attack_behaviour.why_partial_not_catastrophic: Scale=2.0 is insufficient to cause float32 overflow at application model gradient magnitudes. The attack degrades performance but the model continues learning to some degree. Byzantine updates at scale=2.0 contribute negatively to aggregation but legitimate clients (8 out of 10) still outvote them in aggregate.
attack_behaviour.normal_class_resilience: Normal achieves 0.9405 F1 under attack — Byzantine clients do not significantly disrupt the model's ability to identify benign traffic.
attack_behaviour.most_damaged_class: Backdoor drops from 0.6418 (baseline) to 0.2359 (under attack) — 63% relative degradation
attack_behaviour.fingerprinting_damage: Fingerprinting drops from 0.4825 (baseline) to 0.1110 (under attack) — 77% relative degradation

vs_baseline.characterisation: Meaningful degradation — attack measurably harms detection capability without total collapse

vs_network_nodefence.note: Application model is MORE ROBUST under Byzantine attack than network model. This is because scale=2.0 vs 5.0, not because the application model architecture is inherently more robust.

comparison.key_finding: Byzantine attacks at scale=2.0 produce meaningful but recoverable degradation in the application-layer model. The attack is most damaging to rare classes (Backdoor, Fingerprinting) which already have borderline learning signal. This directly motivates Multi-Krum even in the application domain.
